status: controlled small-circle dual-photon mass-gap calculation with an explicit unproved large-circle and R4 continuity gate

setup.spacetime: R3 x S1 with circumference L
setup.deformation: Delta S proportional to L^-3 integral_R3 sum_n a_n |Tr Omega^n|^2 with sufficiently positive coefficients
setup.centerSymmetricHolonomy: Omega has evenly spaced eigenvalues and the long-distance gauge description abelianizes to U(1)^(N-1)
setup.qualification: abelianization is a controlled gauge-fixed infrared description, not spontaneous breaking of a local gauge symmetry

pureDeformedYangMills.leadingObjects: N monopole-instantons associated with the N-1 simple roots and the affine root
pureDeformedYangMills.order: zeta_m proportional to exp(-S0) times a calculable prefactor
pureDeformedYangMills.gapStatement: at theta=0 the Hessian is positive on the SU(N) Cartan subspace

qcdAdjointTemplate.leadingBosonicObjects: magnetic bions with charges alpha_i-alpha_(i+1) when monopole operators carry fermion zero modes
qcdAdjointTemplate.order: zeta_b proportional to exp(-2 S0) times a calculable prefactor
qcdAdjointTemplate.separation: bions are the leading bosonic gap mechanism in QCD(adj), but only a subleading template in pure deformed Yang-Mills where monopoles already contribute

normalization.kineticConvention: the finite witness sets the dual-photon kinetic matrix to the identity
normalization.physicalMassRule: for a general kinetic matrix K_sigma, physical mass-squared eigenvalues are eigenvalues of K_sigma^(-1/2) H K_sigma^(-1/2)
normalization.commonShift: the vector (1,...,1) is a redundant U(1) center-of-mass embedding direction removed by sum_i sigma_i=0; it is not the discrete Z_N center symmetry

combinedNumericalWitness.interpretation: positive mass-squared on every physical dual-photon direction in this canonical normalization

generalAffineSpectrum.fourierModes: sigma_tilde_k=N^-1/2 sum_j exp(-2 pi i k j/N) sigma_j; these diagonalize the cyclic affine-root Hessian
generalAffineSpectrum.modeMeaning: k=0 is the decoupled common-shift photon added by the U(N) embedding and is absent in SU(N); k=1,...,N-1 are the physical dual-photon modes
generalAffineSpectrum.largeN: lambda_min_m ~ 4 pi^2/N^2 and lambda_min_b ~ 16 pi^4/N^4, before the N dependence of fugacities and kinetic normalization
generalAffineSpectrum.uniformityWarning: the dimensionless affine Hessian alone has no N-uniform lower bound, while the semiclassical domain N L Lambda << 1 simultaneously shrinks

semiclassicalPhysicalScale.runningScale: m_gamma=A_tilde Lambda (Lambda N L)^(5/6) |log(Lambda N L)|^(9/11), up to controlled logarithmic corrections and an order-one prefactor
semiclassicalPhysicalScale.limit: at fixed finite N the calculable physical dual-photon gap tends to zero as L tends to zero even while semiclassical control improves
semiclassicalPhysicalScale.consequence: a uniform-continuity proof must start at a finite controlled L0 and bound the gap away from zero on L>=L0; control arbitrarily close to L=0 is not a uniform positive-gap theorem

supported: the center-stabilizing deformation preserves center symmetry at small L
in N L Lambda << 1 the W bosons are parametrically heavier than the dual photons
the dilute monopole gas in pure deformed Yang-Mills generates a calculable positive dual-photon Hessian at theta=0
there is no known local order parameter distinguishing the weakly coupled abelian confinement regime from the large-L strongly coupled confinement regime
notProved: a single path in (L,a_n) from the controlled deformed theory to undeformed Yang-Mills on R4 along which the physical gauge-invariant gap has a strictly positive uniform lower bound
uniform error bounds on the semiclassical expansion as N L Lambda approaches one
Osterwalder-Schrader Schwinger functions and a regulator-independent Hamiltonian for the endpoint theory
that no non-Landau transition, level rearrangement or exponentially closing crossover invalidates gap transport
interchange of the limits volume to infinity, cutoff to zero, L to infinity, deformation to zero and possibly N to infinity
identification of the small-circle dual photon with the lightest R4 glueball through a controlled operator map
continuityGate.necessaryUniformStatement: there must exist Delta_star>0 and a path gamma(s), 0<=s<1, such that the gauge-invariant physical gap Delta[gamma(s)]>=Delta_star uniformly, the Schwinger functions converge as s approaches 1, and the endpoint is undeformed Yang-Mills on R4
continuityGate.absenceOfOrderParameter: same symmetry realization is evidence for possible continuity but is not a spectral inequality

specialLimits.theta: the explicit Hessians are theta=0 witnesses; at theta near pi branch competition and monopole interference require a separate analysis
specialLimits.largeN: volume independence concerns the neutral sector at N=infinity under unbroken center symmetry; it does not turn the finite-N semiclassical Hessian into a constructive R4 gap proof
specialLimits.largeL: when N L Lambda is no longer small, W-boson/dual-photon scale separation and dilute-gas control are lost even if center symmetry remains unbroken

spin23Boundary.useful: this is the most explicit compact nonperturbative gap mechanism available as a laboratory for internal SU(N) sectors and for testing scale-sharing proposals
spin23Boundary.notTransported: the root Hessian, compact duality and positive fugacities do not analytically continue to the noncompact Spin(2,3) gravitational connection
spin23Boundary.gravityConstraint: a viable Spin(2,3) phase must still retain the massless spin-2 sector, so at most selected compact or auxiliary sectors may inherit an analogous gap mechanism

decision: Center-stabilized Yang-Mills supplies a genuine analytically controlled mass gap on small R3 x S1, and its affine-root spectrum can be computed exactly. The route to ordinary R4 Yang-Mills remains a continuity theorem with a uniform physical lower bound, not a further finite Hessian calculation.
